# pigz - Parallel Implementation of GZip

pigz (pronounced "pig-zee") is a parallel implementation of gzip that compresses files using multiple processors and cores.

## What pigz does

pigz is a fully functional replacement for gzip that exploits multiple processors and multiple cores to compress data faster. It can compress and decompress files in gzip, zlib, and zip formats.

## Basic Usage

```
pigz [options] [files...]
unpigz [options] [files...]
```

If no files are specified or "-" is given as a filename, pigz reads from standard input.

## Key Features

- **Parallel compression**: Splits input into chunks (default 128 KB) and compresses them in parallel
- **Multiple output formats**: Supports gzip, zlib, and single-entry zip formats
- **Compatible with gzip**: Can decompress any gzip file; gzip can decompress any pigz-compressed file
- **Independent blocks**: Optional mode for partial error recovery and random access
- **rsyncable**: Optional mode for rsync-friendly output

## Common Options

- **-#** (1-9, 11): Set compression level (1=fastest, 9=best, 11=zopfli for maximum compression)
- **-d, --decompress**: Decompress files
- **-k, --keep**: Keep original files (don't delete after compression)
- **-c, --stdout**: Write output to stdout
- **-p n**: Use n processors (default: all available)
- **-b n**: Set block size to n KB (default: 128)
- **-i, --independent**: Compress blocks independently
- **-R, --rsyncable**: Make output rsync-friendly
- **-l, --list**: List contents of compressed files
- **-t, --test**: Test integrity of compressed files
- **-f, --force**: Force overwrite of output files
- **-r, --recursive**: Recursively compress directories
- **-z, --zlib**: Use zlib format instead of gzip
- **-K, --zip**: Use zip format (single entry)
- **-v, --verbose**: Verbose output
- **-h, --help**: Display help

## Examples

Compress a file using all available processors:
```
pigz file.txt
```

Compress with maximum compression (slower):
```
pigz -11 file.txt
```

Decompress a file:
```
pigz -d file.txt.gz
# or
unpigz file.txt.gz
```

Compress to stdout:
```
pigz -c file.txt > file.txt.gz
```

Compress with 4 processors and keep the original:
```
pigz -k -p 4 file.txt
```

Test compressed file integrity:
```
pigz -t file.txt.gz
```

## Environment Variables

- **GZIP**: Options read from this variable before command line options
- **PIGZ**: Options read from this variable after GZIP but before command line options

## File Formats

pigz produces standard gzip, zlib, or zip format output. Any tool that can decompress these formats can decompress pigz output, and pigz can decompress any standard gzip file.

## Performance

The input is broken into chunks that are compressed in parallel. Each chunk is compressed independently with the last 32K of the previous chunk used as a dictionary to maintain compression effectiveness. The number of threads defaults to the number of available processors.

Decompression uses a single thread for the actual decompression, but creates additional threads for reading, writing, and checksum calculation.

## More Information

For complete documentation, see the pigz man page (pigz.1 or pigz.pdf).

pigz was written by Mark Adler.

.TH PIGZ 1 "August 19, 2023"
.SH NAME
pigz, unpigz \- compress or expand files
.SH SYNOPSIS
.ll +8
.B pigz
.RB [ " \-cdfhikKlLmMnNqrRtz0..9,11 " ]
[
.B -b
.I blocksize
]
[
.B -p
.I threads
]
[
.B -S
.I suffix
]
[
.I "name \&..."
]
.ll -8
.br
.B unpigz
.RB [ " \-cfhikKlLmMnNqrRtz " ]
[
.B -b
.I blocksize
]
[
.B -p
.I threads
]
[
.B -S
.I suffix
]
[
.I "name \&..."
]
.SH DESCRIPTION
.I Pigz
compresses using threads to make use of multiple processors and cores.
The input is broken up into 128 KB chunks with each compressed in parallel.
The individual check value for each chunk is also calculated in parallel.
The compressed data is written in order to the output, and a combined check
value is calculated from the individual check values.
.PP
The compressed data format generated is in the gzip, zlib, or single-entry
zip format using the deflate compression method.  The compression produces
partial raw deflate streams which are concatenated by a single write thread
and wrapped with the appropriate header and trailer, where the trailer
contains the combined check value.
.PP
Each partial raw deflate stream is terminated by an empty stored block
(using the Z_SYNC_FLUSH option of zlib), in order to end that partial bit
stream at a byte boundary.  That allows the partial streams to be
concatenated simply as sequences of bytes.  This adds a very small four to
five byte overhead to the output for each input chunk.
.PP
The default input block size is 128K, but can be changed with the
.B -b
option.  The number of compress threads is set by default to the number
of online processors,
which can be changed using the
.B -p
option.  Specifying
.B -p 1
avoids the use of threads entirely.
.PP
The input blocks, while compressed independently, have the last 32K of the
previous block loaded as a preset dictionary to preserve the compression
effectiveness of deflating in a single thread.  This can be turned off using
the
.B -i
or
.B --independent
option, so that the blocks can be decompressed
independently for partial error recovery or for random access. This also
inserts an extra empty block to flag independent blocks by prefacing
each with the nine-byte sequence (in hex): 00 00 FF FF 00 00 00 FF FF.
.PP
Decompression can't be parallelized, at least not without specially prepared
deflate streams for that purpose.  As a result,
.I pigz
uses a single thread
(the main thread) for decompression, but will create three other threads for
reading, writing, and check calculation, which can speed up decompression
under some circumstances.  Parallel decompression can be turned off by
specifying one process
(
.B -dp 1
or
.B -tp 1
).
.PP
All options on the command line are processed before any names are processed.
If no names are provided on the command line, or if "-" is given as a name (but
not after "--"), then the input is taken from stdin. If the GZIP or PIGZ
environment variables are set, then options are taken from their values before
any command line options are processed, first from GZIP, then from PIGZ.
.PP
Compressed files can be restored to their original form using
.I pigz -d
or
.I unpigz.

.SH OPTIONS
.TP
.B -# --fast --best
Regulate the speed of compression using the specified digit
.IR # ,
where
.B \-1
or
.B \-\-fast
indicates the fastest compression method (less compression)
and
.B \-9
or
.B \-\-best
indicates the slowest compression method (best compression).
.B -0
is no compression.
.B \-11
gives a few percent better compression at a severe cost in execution time,
using the zopfli algorithm by Jyrki Alakuijala.
The default is
.B \-6.
.TP
.B -A --alias xxx
Use xxx as the name for any --zip entry from stdin (the default name is "-").
.TP
.B -b --blocksize mmm
Set compression block size to mmmK (default 128KiB).
.TP
.B -c --stdout --to-stdout
Write all processed output to stdout (won't delete).
.TP
.B -C --comment ccc
Include the provided comment in the gzip header or zip central file header.
.TP
.B -d --decompress --uncompress
Decompress the compressed input.
.TP
.B -f --force
Force overwrite, compress .gz, links, and to terminal.
.TP
.B -h --help
Display a help screen and quit.
.TP
.B -H --huffman
Compress using the Huffman-only strategy.
.TP
.B -i --independent
Compress blocks independently for damage recovery.
.TP
.B -k --keep
Do not delete original file after processing.
.TP
.B -K --zip
Compress to PKWare zip (.zip) single entry format.
.TP
.B -l --list
List the contents of the compressed input.
.TP
.B -L --license
Display the
.I pigz
license and quit.
.TP
.B -m --no-time
Do not store or restore the modification time. -Nm will store or restore the
name, but not the modification time. Note that the order of the options is
important.
.TP
.B -M --time
Store or restore the modification time. -nM will store or restore the
modification time, but not the name. Note that the order of the options is
important. Modification times are stored only for regular files, not pipes.
.TP
.B -n --no-name
Do not store or restore the file name or the modification time. This is the
default when decompressing. When the file name is not restored from the header,
the name of the compressed file with the suffix stripped is the name of the
decompressed file. When the modification time is not restored from the header,
the modification time of the compressed file is used (not the current time).
.TP
.B -N --name
Store or restore both the file name and the modification time. This is the
default when compressing.
.TP
.B -p --processes n
Allow up to n processes (default is the number of online processors)
.TP
.B -q --quiet --silent
Print no messages, even on error.
.TP
.B -r --recursive
Process the contents of all subdirectories.
.TP
.B -R --rsyncable
Input-determined block locations for rsync.
.TP
.B -S --suffix .sss
Use suffix .sss instead of .gz (for compression).
.TP
.B -t --test
Test the integrity of the compressed input.
.TP
.B -U --rle
Compress using the run length encoding strategy.
.TP
.B -v --verbose
Provide more verbose output.
.TP
.B -V --version
Show the version of pigz. -vV also shows the zlib version.
.TP
.B -z --zlib
Compress to zlib (.zz) instead of gzip format.
.TP
.B --
All arguments after "--" are treated as file names (for names that start with "-")
.TP
These options are unique to the -11 compression level:
.TP
.B -F  --first
Do iterations first, before block split (default is last).
.TP
.B -I, --iterations n
Number of iterations for optimization (default 15).
.TP
.B -J, --maxsplits n
Maximum number of split blocks (default 15).
.TP
.B -O  --oneblock
Do not split into smaller blocks (default is block splitting).

import subprocess, os, zlib, gzip, hashlib
EXE=os.path.abspath("./executable")
def run(args, inp):
    r=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True)
    if r.returncode!=0:
        print("ERR",args,r.returncode,r.stderr)
    return r.stdout

# compare small input to zlib raw
data=b"hello world\n"*100
for level in [0,1,6,9]:
    out=run([f"-{level}","-c","-n"], data)
    # parse gzip header 10 bytes, trailer 8
    print(level, out[:10], out[-8:])
    raw=out[10:-8]
    # python zlib raw
    co=zlib.compressobj(level, zlib.DEFLATED, -15)
    praw=co.compress(data)+co.flush()
    print("  match python raw?", raw==praw, len(raw), len(praw))
    if raw!=praw:
        print(raw[:50], praw[:50])

# varying p for large
data=os.urandom(1000)  # incompressible? better structured
data=(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"*10000)[:300000]  # 300k
for p in ["1","2","4","8"]:
    out=run(["-c","-n","-p",p], data)
    print("p",p,len(out), hashlib.md5(out).hexdigest())
for b in ["32","128","512"]:
    out=run(["-c","-n","-p","1","-b",b], data)
    print("b p1",b,len(out), hashlib.md5(out).hexdigest())
    out=run(["-c","-n","-p","4","-b",b], data)
    print("b p4",b,len(out), hashlib.md5(out).hexdigest())

# independent
for extra in [[],["-i"],["-R"]]:
    out=run(["-c","-n"]+extra, data)
    print(extra, len(out), hashlib.md5(out).hexdigest())
PY

EXE=os.path.abspath("./executable")
def run(args, inp):

    if last:
        return co.compress(blk)+co.flush(zlib.Z_FINISH)
    else:
        return co.compress(blk)+co.flush(zlib.Z_SYNC_FLUSH)

EXE=os.path.abspath("./executable")
def run(args, inp):
    return subprocess.run([EXE]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True).stdout

def candidates(data, blk_idx, block=32768):
    blk=data[blk_idx*block:(blk_idx+1)*block]
    zdict=data[max(0,blk_idx*block-32768):blk_idx*block] if blk_idx>0 else b""
    outs={}
    for name,mode in [("sync",zlib.Z_SYNC_FLUSH),("partial",zlib.Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH),("finish",zlib.Z_FINISH),("block",5),("full",zlib.Z_FULL_FLUSH)]:
        co=zlib.compressobj(6,zlib.DEFLATED,-15,zdict=zdict)
        outs[name]=co.compress(blk)+co.flush(mode)
    return outs

for name,data in [("pattern",b"abcd"*20000),("hello",b"hello world\n"*6000),("a",b"a"*70000)]:
    raw=run(["-c","-n","-b","32"],data)[10:-8]
    print("\n",name,"raw len",len(raw))
    n=(len(data)+32767)//32768
    for i in range(n):
        cand=candidates(data,i)
        for k,v in cand.items():
            pos=raw.find(v)
            # also first byte modified (clear/set BFINAL)
            v2=bytes([v[0]^1])+v[1:]
            pos2=raw.find(v2)

            mid=v[5:-5] if len(v)>10 else v
            posmid=raw.find(mid)
            print(f" block{i} {k:8} len={len(v)} find={pos} find_bfinalflip={pos2} find_mid={posmid} head={v[:6].hex()} tail={v[-8:].hex()}")
    print("raw hex",raw.hex())

    Before the call of deflate(), the application should ensure that at least
  one of the actions is possible, by providing more input and/or consuming more
  output, and updating avail_in or avail_out accordingly; avail_out should
  never be zero before the call.  The application can consume the compressed
  output when it wants, for example when the output buffer is full (avail_out
  == 0), or after each call of deflate().  If deflate returns Z_OK and with
  zero avail_out, it must be called again after making room in the output
  buffer because there might be more output pending. See deflatePending(),
  which can be used if desired to determine whether or not there is more ouput
  in that case.

    Normally the parameter flush is set to Z_NO_FLUSH, which allows deflate to
  decide how much data to accumulate before producing output, in order to
  maximize compression.

    If the parameter flush is set to Z_SYNC_FLUSH, all pending output is
  flushed to the output buffer and the output is aligned on a byte boundary, so
  that the decompressor can get all input data available so far.  (In
  particular avail_in is zero after the call if enough output space has been
  provided before the call.) Flushing may degrade compression for some
  compression algorithms and so it should be used only when necessary.  This
  completes the current deflate block and follows it with an empty stored block
  that is three bits plus filler bits to the next byte, followed by four bytes
  (00 00 ff ff).

    If flush is set to Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH, all pending output is flushed to the
  output buffer, but the output is not aligned to a byte boundary.  All of the
  input data so far will be available to the decompressor, as for Z_SYNC_FLUSH.
  This completes the current deflate block and follows it with an empty fixed
  codes block that is 10 bits long.  This assures that enough bytes are output
  in order for the decompressor to finish the block before the empty fixed
  codes block.

    If flush is set to Z_BLOCK, a deflate block is completed and emitted, as
  for Z_SYNC_FLUSH, but the output is not aligned on a byte boundary, and up to
  seven bits of the current block are held to be written as the next byte after
  the next deflate block is completed.  In this case, the decompressor may not
  be provided enough bits at this point in order to complete decompression of
  the data provided so far to the compressor.  It may need to wait for the next
  block to be emitted.  This is for advanced applications that need to control
  the emission of deflate blocks.

    If flush is set to Z_FULL_FLUSH, all output is flushed as with
  Z_SYNC_FLUSH, and the compression state is reset so that decompression can
  restart from this point if previous compressed data has been damaged or if
  random access is desired.  Using Z_FULL_FLUSH too often can seriously degrade
  compression.

    If deflate returns with avail_out == 0, this function must be called again
  with the same value of the flush parameter and more output space (updated
  avail_out), until the flush is complete (deflate returns with non-zero
  avail_out).  In the case of a Z_FULL_FLUSH or Z_SYNC_FLUSH, make sure that
  avail_out is greater than six to avoid repeated flush markers due to
  avail_out == 0 on return.

    If the parameter flush is set to Z_FINISH, pending input is processed,
  pending output is flushed and deflate returns with Z_STREAM_END if there was
  enough output space.  If deflate returns with Z_OK or Z_BUF_ERROR, this
  function must be called again with Z_FINISH and more output space (updated
  avail_out) but no more input data, until it returns with Z_STREAM_END or an
  error.  After deflate has returned Z_STREAM_END, the only possible operations
  on the stream are deflateReset or deflateEnd.

    Z_FINISH can be used in the first deflate call after deflateInit if all the
  compression is to be done in a single step.  In order to complete in one
  call, avail_out must be at least the value returned by deflateBound (see
  below).  Then deflate is guaranteed to return Z_STREAM_END.  If not enough
  output space is provided, deflate will not return Z_STREAM_END, and it must
  be called again as described above.

    deflate() sets strm->adler to the Adler-32 checksum of all input read
  so far (that is, total_in bytes).  If a gzip stream is being generated, then
  strm->adler will be the CRC-32 checksum of the input read so far.  (See

  the input data type (Z_BINARY or Z_TEXT).  If in doubt, the data is
  considered binary.  This field is only for information purposes and does not
  affect the compression algorithm in any manner.

  processed or more output produced), Z_STREAM_END if all input has been
  consumed and all output has been produced (only when flush is set to
  Z_FINISH), Z_STREAM_ERROR if the stream state was inconsistent (for example

  avail_in or avail_out was zero).  Note that Z_BUF_ERROR is not fatal, and

import ast, zlib
data=open("/tmp/rsync_data.bin","rb").read()
bounds=ast.literal_eval(open("/tmp/rsync_bounds_true.txt").read())
pos=bounds[1:-1]  # exclude 0 and EOF 200000 (last in true list is 200000)
# True list generated with -i includes final 200000; boundaries internal = [1:-1]
print("positives",len(pos),pos[:5])

def maxk(vals):
    k=0
    for bit in range(16):
        b=vals[0]>>bit &1
        if all(((v>>bit)&1)==b for v in vals):
            # check contiguous low bits only: we need all low bits up to k match
            pass
        else:
            break
        k+=1
    return k

results=[]
def test(name, vals):
    k=maxk(vals)
    if k>=7:
        results.append((k,name,vals[0] & ((1<<k)-1)))
        print("hit",k,name,vals[:3])

# trailing CRC / adler / FNV etc
for N in [4,8,12,16,20,24,32,48,64,128]:
    test(f"crc32 N={N}", [zlib.crc32(data[b-N:b]) for b in pos])
    test(f"adler N={N}", [zlib.adler32(data[b-N:b]) for b in pos])
    # fnv1a 32
    vals=[]
    for b in pos:
        h=2166136261
        for c in data[b-N:b]:
            h ^= c; h=(h*16777619)&0xffffffff
        vals.append(h)
    test(f"fnv1a N={N}", vals)
    vals=[]
    for b in pos:
        h=2166136261
        for c in data[b-N:b]:
            h=(h*16777619)&0xffffffff; h ^= c
        vals.append(h)
    test(f"fnv1 N={N}", vals)

Ps=list(range(3,300,2))+[257,263,271,277,281,283,293,307,512+45,65599 & 0xffff, 131,65521%1000]
for N in [3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,12,16,20,24,32,48,64]:
    windows=[data[b-N:b] for b in pos]
    for P in Ps:
        for variant in range(4):
            vals=[]
            for w in windows:
                h=0
                if variant==0:
                    for c in w: h=(h*P + c)&0xffffffff
                elif variant==1:
                    for c in w: h=(h*P ^ c)&0xffffffff
                elif variant==2:
                    for c in reversed(w): h=(h*P + c)&0xffffffff
                else:
                    for c in w: h=(h*P + c + 1)&0xffffffff
                vals.append(h)
            test(f"poly N={N} P={P} v={variant}", vals)
    print("done N",N,"results",results[-5:] if results else None)

import ast
data=open("/tmp/rsync_big.bin","rb").read()
bounds=ast.literal_eval(open("/tmp/rsync_big_bounds.txt").read())
pos=bounds[1:-1]

def window_int(b,N):
    # bit j corresponds to ? we'll just pack bytes from oldest to newest as big integer bits: byte offset from end?
    v=0
    # bit position: for byte index i=0 oldest ... N-1 newest, bit = i*8+bitinbyte
    for i,byte in enumerate(data[b-N:b]):
        v |= byte << (i*8)
    return v

def rank_nullity(rows, nbits):
    basis={}
    rank=0
    for r in rows:
        x=r
        while x:
            piv=x.bit_length()-1
            if piv in basis:
                x ^= basis[piv]
            else:
                basis[piv]=x; rank+=1; break
    return rank, nbits-rank, basis

for N in [2,4,6,8,10,12,16,20,24,32,40,48]:
    ws=[window_int(b,N) for b in pos]
    diffs=[w ^ ws[0] for w in ws[1:]]
    rank,nullity,_=rank_nullity(diffs,N*8)
    print(f"N={N} bits={N*8} examples={len(ws)} rank_diffs={rank} nullity={nullity}")

    for i,byte in enumerate(data[b-N:b]): # i 0 oldest, N-1 newest
        v |= byte << (i*8)
    return v

def nullspace(rows,nbits):
    # rows are vectors (diffs). Find basis w such that dot(w,row)=0 for all.
    # Gaussian elimination to row echelon on rows, tracking pivots.
    rows=list(rows)
    pivots=[]
    r=0
    # Matrix as list ints; perform elimination choosing highest bit? Let's do standard by columns 0..nbits-1
    # Convert to list and do elimination for pivot column scanning 0..nbits-1
    mat=rows[:]
    pivot_cols=[]
    where=[-1]*nbits
    row=0
    for col in range(nbits):
        # find pivot row >=row with bit col
        sel=-1
        for i in range(row,len(mat)):
            if (mat[i]>>col)&1:
                sel=i; break
        if sel==-1: continue
        mat[row],mat[sel]=mat[sel],mat[row]
        where[col]=row
        for i in range(len(mat)):
            if i!=row and ((mat[i]>>col)&1):
                mat[i] ^= mat[row]

        for c in pivot_cols:
            # row where[c] has equation sum_{?} ??? We need solve A w=0: for each pivot col, w_c = sum over free (A[row][free] * w_free)
            rrow=where[c]
            if (mat[rrow]>>f)&1:
                w |= 1<<c
        basis.append(w)
    return basis,free,pivot_cols,mat,where

def parity(x): return bin(x).count("1")&1

import zlib, struct
def manual_gz(data=b"hello", name=None, comment=None, mtime=0, extra=None, osbyte=3, xfl=0):
    flg=0
    if extra is not None: flg|=4
    if name is not None: flg|=8
    if comment is not None: flg|=16
    hdr=struct.pack("<BBBBLBB",0x1f,0x8b,8,flg,mtime,xfl,osbyte)
    if extra is not None: hdr+=struct.pack("<H",len(extra))+extra
    if name is not None:
        if isinstance(name,str): name=name.encode()
        hdr+=name+b"\0"
    if comment is not None:
        if isinstance(comment,str): comment=comment.encode()
        hdr+=comment+b"\0"
    # no FHCRC handling in this builder unless manually add elsewhere
    co=zlib.compressobj(6,zlib.DEFLATED,-15)
    raw=co.compress(data)+co.flush()
    trailer=struct.pack("<II",zlib.crc32(data)&0xffffffff,len(data)&0xffffffff)
    return hdr+raw+trailer

import pty, os, subprocess, shutil, time, select, errno
EXE=os.path.abspath("./executable"); B="/tmp/pigzpty"
def run_pty(answer, args=["a.txt"], timeout=3):
    shutil.rmtree(B,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(B)
    open(B+"/a.txt","wb").write(b"new data")
    open(B+"/a.txt.gz","wb").write(b"old output")
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    p=subprocess.Popen([EXE]+args,cwd=B,stdin=slave,stdout=slave,stderr=slave,close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    out=b""; sent=False; start=time.time()
    while time.time()-start<timeout:
        r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.1)
        if r:
            try:
                chunk=os.read(master,4096)
            except OSError:
                break
            if not chunk: break
            out+=chunk
            if (b"overwrite" in out or b"?" in out) and not sent:
                os.write(master,answer); sent=True
        if p.poll() is not None:
            # drain
            try:
                while True:
                    chunk=os.read(master,4096)
                    if not chunk: break
                    out+=chunk
            except: pass
            break
    if p.poll() is None:
        p.kill(); p.wait()
    os.close(master)
    files={f:open(B+"/"+f,"rb").read()[:40] for f in sorted(os.listdir(B))}
    print("args",args,"answer",answer,"exit",p.returncode,"ptyout",out,"sent",sent,"files",files)

for ans in [b"y\n",b"n\n",b"Y\n",b"yes\n",b"\n",b"q\n",b" y\n"]:
    run_pty(ans)

import subprocess,os,sys,struct,zlib

 r=subprocess.run([EXE,"-lv"],input=data,capture_output=True); lines=r.stdout.decode().splitlines(); print(label,"total",len(data),"rc",r.returncode,lines[-1] if len(lines)>1 else r.stdout, r.stderr.decode().strip())
g1=manual_gz(b"hello ",name="a.txt",mtime=111111111)
# trailing junk lengths / patterns
for junk in [b"j",b"ju",b"jun",b"junk",b"junk1",b"junk12",b"junk123",b"junk1234",b"junk12345",b"\0"*1,b"\0"*4,b"\0"*8,b"\0"*9,b"\0"*20,b"12345678",b"123456789"]:
 lst(g1+junk,f"junk={junk!r}")
print("multi varied")
for d2 in [b"",b"x",b"world",b"a"*1000]:
 g2=manual_gz(d2,name="b.txt")
 lst(g1+g2,f"second len {len(d2)}")
for d3 in [b"third"]:
 lst(g1+manual_gz(b"second",name="b")+manual_gz(d3,name="c"),"three members")
print("corrupt ISIZE single")
for isize in [0,1,5,6,100,100000,4294967295]:
 d=bytearray(g1); d[-4:]=struct.pack("<I",isize); lst(bytes(d),f"isize {isize}")
print("truncate gzip after header counts")
for n in range(16,33):
 lst(g1[:n],f"trunc{n}")

import sys,zlib,subprocess,os
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from manual_gz import manual_gz
EXE=os.path.abspath("./executable")
def analyze(label,data):
  r=subprocess.run([EXE,"-l"],input=data,capture_output=True)
  line=r.stdout.decode().splitlines()[-1] if r.stdout else r.stderr.decode()
  # gzip header len find manually g1 header16 in all cases starting g1 (except zlib)
  body=data[16:-8] if data[:2]==b'\x1f\x8b' else data[2:-4] if data[:1]==b'x' else b''
  d=zlib.decompressobj(-15)
  try:
    out=d.decompress(body); out+=d.flush(); status=f"eof={d.eof} unused={len(d.unused_data)} unconsumed={len(d.unconsumed_tail)} outlen={len(out)}"
  except Exception as e:
    status=f"err {e} out?"
  print(label,"list:",line.strip()," | inflate bodylen",len(body),status)

g1=manual_gz(b"hello ",name="a.txt")
analyze("single",g1)
for junk in [b"junk",b"junk12345",b"\0"*8,b"\0"*4]:
 analyze(f"junk{junk!r}",g1+junk)
for d2 in [b"",b"x",b"world",b"a"*100,b"a"*1000,bytes(range(256))*2]:
 analyze(f"second {len(d2)}",g1+manual_gz(d2,name="b.txt"))
# single gzip with lots of incompressible original e.g. 100 bytes random-ish stored deflate ratio >?
import random
rnd=random.Random(0); data=bytes(rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(100))
analyze("single random100",manual_gz(data,name="a.txt"))
analyze("single hello repeated trunc trailer isize weird",manual_gz(b"hello"))
PY
python3 /tmp/list_inflate_corr.py
"}

  for i in range(n): bits.append((v>>i)&1)
 def put_code(v,n): # Huffman code stored as integer canonical value, emit MSB first
  for i in range(n-1,-1,-1): bits.append((v>>i)&1)
 put_lsb(1,1); put_lsb(1,2) # BFINAL=1, BTYPE fixed: bits for type value 1 LSB first = 1,0

/*
ZEXTERN int ZEXPORT inflateBackInit OF((z_streamp strm, int windowBits,
                                        unsigned char FAR *window));

     Initialize the internal stream state for decompression using inflateBack()
   calls.  The fields zalloc, zfree and opaque in strm must be initialized
   before the call.  If zalloc and zfree are Z_NULL, then the default library-
   derived memory allocation routines are used.  windowBits is the base two
   logarithm of the window size, in the range 8..15.  window is a caller
   supplied buffer of that size.  Except for special applications where it is
   assured that deflate was used with small window sizes, windowBits must be 15
   and a 32K byte window must be supplied to be able to decompress general
   deflate streams.

     See inflateBack() for the usage of these routines.

     inflateBackInit will return Z_OK on success, Z_STREAM_ERROR if any of
   the parameters are invalid, Z_MEM_ERROR if the internal state could not be
   allocated, or Z_VERSION_ERROR if the version of the library does not match
   the version of the header file.
*/

typedef unsigned (*in_func) OF((void FAR *,
                                z_const unsigned char FAR * FAR *));
typedef int (*out_func) OF((void FAR *, unsigned char FAR *, unsigned));

ZEXTERN int ZEXPORT inflateBack OF((z_streamp strm,
                                    in_func in, void FAR *in_desc,
                                    out_func out, void FAR *out_desc));
/*
     inflateBack() does a raw inflate with a single call using a call-back
   interface for input and output.  This is potentially more efficient than
   inflate() for file i/o applications, in that it avoids copying between the
   output and the sliding window by simply making the window itself the output
   buffer.  inflate() can be faster on modern CPUs when used with large
   buffers.  inflateBack() trusts the application to not change the output
   buffer passed by the output function, at least until inflateBack() returns.

     inflateBackInit() must be called first to allocate the internal state
   and to initialize the state with the user-provided window buffer.
   inflateBack() may then be used multiple times to inflate a complete, raw
   deflate stream with each call.  inflateBackEnd() is then called to free the
   allocated state.

     A raw deflate stream is one with no zlib or gzip header or trailer.
   This routine would normally be used in a utility that reads zip or gzip
   files and writes out uncompressed files.  The utility would decode the
   header and process the trailer on its own, hence this routine expects only
   the raw deflate stream to decompress.  This is different from the default
   behavior of inflate(), which expects a zlib header and trailer around the
   deflate stream.

     inflateBack() uses two subroutines supplied by the caller that are then
   called by inflateBack() for input and output.  inflateBack() calls those
   routines until it reads a complete deflate stream and writes out all of the
   uncompressed data, or until it encounters an error.  The function's
   parameters and return types are defined above in the in_func and out_func
   typedefs.  inflateBack() will call in(in_desc, &buf) which should return the
   number of bytes of provided input, and a pointer to that input in buf.  If
   there is no input available, in() must return zero -- buf is ignored in that
   case -- and inflateBack() will return a buffer error.  inflateBack() will
   call out(out_desc, buf, len) to write the uncompressed data buf[0..len-1].
   out() should return zero on success, or non-zero on failure.  If out()
   returns non-zero, inflateBack() will return with an error.  Neither in() nor
   out() are permitted to change the contents of the window provided to
   inflateBackInit(), which is also the buffer that out() uses to write from.
   The length written by out() will be at most the window size.  Any non-zero
   amount of input may be provided by in().

     For convenience, inflateBack() can be provided input on the first call by
   setting strm->next_in and strm->avail_in.  If that input is exhausted, then
   in() will be called.  Therefore strm->next_in must be initialized before
   calling inflateBack().  If strm->next_in is Z_NULL, then in() will be called
   immediately for input.  If strm->next_in is not Z_NULL, then strm->avail_in
   must also be initialized, and then if strm->avail_in is not zero, input will
   initially be taken from strm->next_in[0 ..  strm->avail_in - 1].

     The in_desc and out_desc parameters of inflateBack() is passed as the
   first parameter of in() and out() respectively when they are called.  These
   descriptors can be optionally used to pass any information that the caller-
   supplied in() and out() functions need to do their job.

     On return, inflateBack() will set strm->next_in and strm->avail_in to
   pass back any unused input that was provided by the last in() call.  The
   return values of inflateBack() can be Z_STREAM_END on success, Z_BUF_ERROR
   if in() or out() returned an error, Z_DATA_ERROR if there was a format error
   in the deflate stream (in which case strm->msg is set to indicate the nature
   of the error), or Z_STREAM_ERROR if the stream was not properly initialized.
   In the case of Z_BUF_ERROR, an input or output error can be distinguished
   using strm->next_in which will be Z_NULL only if in() returned an error.  If
   strm->next_in is not Z_NULL, then the Z_BUF_ERROR was due to out() returning
   non-zero.  (in() will always be called before out(), so strm->next_in is
   assured to be defined if out() returns non-zero.)  Note that inflateBack()
   cannot return Z_OK.
*/

cat > compile.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
# Build the pigz reimplementation. zlib development files are required;
# try to install them if they are missing and a package manager is usable.
if [ ! -f /usr/include/zlib.h ]; then
    if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        apt-get update -qq >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        apt-get install -y -qq zlib1g-dev gcc >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi
fi
CC="${CC:-cc}"
"$CC" -O2 -std=gnu11 -Wall -o executable pigz.c -lz -lm -pthread
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh
rm -rf /tmp/isolated2 && mkdir /tmp/isolated2 && cp pigz.c compile.sh /tmp/isolated2/ && sh -c 'cd /tmp && /tmp/isolated2/compile.sh && /tmp/isolated2/executable -V && printf hello | /tmp/isolated2/executable | /tmp/isolated2/executable -dc'
git add compile.sh && git commit -m "Make build script location-independent" 2>&1 | tail -2

  print(name,flushname,"len",len(out),"common prefix",common,"head",out[:12].hex())

def sustained(flushmode):

  flush=flushmode if i < len(bounds)-2 else zlib.Z_FINISH
